title: Night Commons — Handoff Codex
content:
Quick context
- Shift: 22:00 - 06:00 PT (me, Asha). Mate0 checked in 22:30 for GPU pool health sweep.
- Primary focus tonight: 2 small customer-facing incidents and a recurring tail-latency blip on hosted-api/model-x-13b.

Snapshot at 23:55
- Hosted API: overall traffic normal (~230rps), but P95 token latency for model-x-13b elevated to 720ms (baseline ~320ms).
- Dedicated pools: healthy; one node in pool-east-2 shows elevated GPU mem usage (95%) and occasional OOM kills this evening.
- KV cache hit rate for model-x-13b: 62% (baseline ~78%). Sudden drop correlates with a rollout at ~21:40 (version v2.3.1 -> v2.4.rc).

Incidents (active)
1) INC-RW-1276: model-x-13b tail latency spike (high severity for affected customers) — Mitigated w/ temporary routing to model-x-13b-quant (lower quality, lower latency).
   - Timeline: spike started 21:50 after rollout, triaged 22:15, temporary route created 23:05.
   - Next step: revert rollout if root cause is kernel selection mismatch.
   - Notes: regression tests on PR #1189 showed minor perf variance but not this magnitude.

2) INC-RW-1289: dedicated-node-5 frequent process restarts in pool-east-2.
   - Cause hypothesis: nightly batch job (checkpoint-compact) colliding with inference workloads -> memory pressure.
   - Temporary action: cordon node and move traffic to pool-east-2-burst. Ticket created (JIRA-RW-3438).

Triage checklist (what I did / what to do)
- Observed metrics: p95_token_latency, tail_latency_99, kv_cache_hit_rate, gpu_mem_used_pct, runtime_errors_per_min.
- Quick dashboards: Datadog "Hosted API -> model-x-13b" + Kibana logs index runtime-logs-*/model-x-13b.
- Commands I ran (keep handy):
   * Check pods: kubectl -n serving get pods -l model=model-x-13b -o wide
   * Logs (recent high-lat node): kubectl -n serving logs pod/model-x-13b-runtime-7f8 -c runtime --since=2h | grep -i "kv cache" -n -B2 -A3
   * Kill runaway worker (last resort): kubectl -n serving exec -it pod/... -- bash -c "pkill -f runtime_worker && sleep 20 && supervisorctl status"
   * Re-route rule (console CLI): rwdctl routing set host:hosted --model model-x-13b --variant model-x-13b-quant --weight 100 --note "temp fallback during tail latency"
- Rollback plan: if after reverting kernel selection / rollout -> no improvement, escalate to runtime core. To revert rollout: rwdctl deploy rollback model-x-13b --to v2.3.1 and monitor for 15min.

Temporary runbook snippets (notes / scratch)
- If KV cache hit rate drops >15% relative baseline and tail_latency_99 > 1s: prefer routing to quant variant or warm cache via replay job.
- Re-warm cache: run small replay job against prefix-heavy queries (script: infra/tools/kv-rewarm.sh --model model-x-13b --duration 5m). Watch traffic and token cost.
- If GPU mem > 93% on a node: cordon node and drain (kubectl cordon <node>; rwdctl pool rebalance --pool pool-east-2). If restart loop persists, collect core dump (see collection steps below).

Core dump collection (if needed)
1) kubectl -n serving exec -it <pod> -- bash
2) cd /var/log/runtime; sudo gcore -o /tmp/runtime-core $(pidof runtime)
3) scp /tmp/runtime-core* ops@artifact-uploader:/incoming/cores/<date>/
4) attach link to JIRA and ping @Chen Li in #sre-urgent

Escalation contacts
- First: Mateo Ruiz (pager) / Slack: @mateo (SRE)
- Runtime lead: Chen Li (on-call pager) / Slack: @chenli-runtime
- Oncall manager (after 30m unresolved P1): Priya Srinivasan (pager)

Notes for next shift (things to pick up)
- Follow-up on INC-RW-1276: either rollback PR #1189 or confirm kernel-selection tweak merged tomorrow morning. Add perf snapshot to incident.
- Node health: dedicated-node-5 cordoned, ensure replacement pool autoscaled successfully during night burst window (monitor pool-east-2-burst).
- KV rewarm job scheduled for 02:30 to see if hit rate recovers; watch for cost blast.
- Customer comms: draft posted in INC-RW-1276, wait for confirmed root cause before sending broad notice.

Open questions / TODOs (scratch)
- Why did rollout at 21:40 cause KV cache hit rate to drop? hypothesis: new kernel path uses slightly different input hashing -> cache miss. Need to verify with runtime team.
- Add metric: kv_cache_hash_version (so we can detect cache-shape mismatches across versions).
- Short term: think about automating fallback rule creation when tail_latency_99 exceeds threshold for 5+ minutes.

Postmortem skeleton (if this becomes P1)
- Title: "21:40 rollout -> tail latency spike for model-x-13b"
- Timeline, root cause, detection, mitigation, rollback, follow-ups (owners).

Rough scribbles /brain dump
- If we want to avoid future rollouts causing cold-KV problems: consider a staggered rollout with cache-warm probes (traffic shadowing + warm jobs).
- Cost note: rewarm job will add ~0.5M tokens/hr at current scale; coordinate w/ billing if run >30m.

Misc helpful links (internal)
- Datadog dashboard: https://app.datadoghq.com/dash/1234/hosted-api-model-x-13b
- Kibana: https://kibana.redwood.com/app/discover#/?index=runtime-logs-*
- Incident ticket: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/RW-1276
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1189

Parting note to next oncall
- If you see intermittent high tail latency, first check KV cache hit rate and whether there's an active rollout. Don't escalate immediately — try routing to quant variant for 10-20m while we investigate. If routing doesn't help, escalate to runtime lead.

-- Asha (night)
summary: Night shift notes: two active incidents (tail latency + dedicated node restarts). Temporary routing to quant variant applied; node cordoned. Rewarm job scheduled. Rollback/PR under investigation.
